items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: When did you play with Bunk? You say first in the Eagle Band a little bit way back? ... That one was in the Banner Band.

ctx.x: What style did he play? Something like Louie or Bunk?

He had a big tone, most people say. Oh, it was a much more powerful man, but that style. That style, mm-hmm. When you went to Chicago, what was that date that tells here on this contract? That's April 1917. That's correct. Who all was in that band?

items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: The old Redback Bucking. Oh, he had one. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry I didn't go. I could have gone.

ctx.x: Classe Roy. Roy. R-O-Y. R-O-Y. And who's the bass player? John Sandis. John Sandis. That was a big band. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

New Orleans couldn't come in in New Iberia then. You really like that band? Oh yeah, we killed New Orleans. I mean, we killed till it's there. Don't come in New Iberia, not there when we was there. Now, don't Bunk always want to play with you again? The last few years. Bill Bucking, that last album, he came right here. Two or three times. Flood Rain. You know, you know, the old one can play those numbers on the one. He named him. All the more, the only one. The old Redback Bucking. Oh, he had one. I'm sorry. I'm…
Yes, sir. Sometimes, well, either way, you've been here and been happy.
